backup.title: Backup
backup.description: Download this whole Project (work items, sprints, docs, comments, attachments, statuses, labels) as a single ZIP file.
backup.restoreSpaceHint: Creates a new Project from a backup you made earlier. Nothing existing is overwritten.

backup.newName: New Project name (defaults to the backup’s)

promoteEpic.title: Convert {{key}} to an Epic?
promoteEpic.body: This Task becomes an Epic. An Epic has no parent, sprint, hour estimate, completion percentage or recurrence: if it sits under an Epic it is detached, if it is in a sprint it leaves the sprint, and those fields are cleared. Its Sub-Tasks become Tasks and stay under the Epic. You can rename the Epic below. This cannot be undone.
promoteEpic.name: Name of the Epic

rolesPage.title: Roles and permissions
rolesPage.subtitle: Decide what each role can do. Changes apply immediately.

scopeHelp.SPACE: Project roles apply inside one Project (Product Owner, Developer…). Owners and Admins always have every Project permission.
scopeHelp.WORKSPACE: Workspace roles apply to the whole workspace. Custom roles behave like a Member with the permissions you tick.

rolesPage.name: Name

rolesPage.resetDone: {{name}} was reset to its default permissions.

rolesPage.deleteInUse: {{count}} people use this role. Choose the role they get instead.

share.overrideHint: Saving creates separate settings for this item and the items under it.

state.custom: Custom access: the people below get the chosen role on this item and everything under it, on top of their Project role.

bugs.title: Bugs

bugs.reported: {{key}} reported. The team has been notified.

mailTest.title: Email delivery
mailTest.help: Enter the SMTP details for outgoing email (invitations, password resets, notifications) here; no file editing on the server. The password is stored encrypted and never shown again.
mailTest.okBody: It should arrive within seconds; if not, check your Spam folder.
mailTest.failTitle: The email could not be sent.

hint.passEmpty: The SMTP password is empty. Enter it in the Password field above (for Gmail, a 16-letter “App password”) and save.
hint.auth: The username or password was rejected. Gmail does not accept your normal password; turn on 2-step verification, create a 16-letter App password and enter it in the Password field above.
hint.network: Could not reach the SMTP server. Check the server name and port (Gmail: smtp.gmail.com, 587); some hosts block outgoing 587/465.
hint.host: The SMTP host name could not be resolved. Check the SMTP server spelling above and the server’s DNS access.
hint.rejected: The server rejected the sender or recipient address. The sender address must belong to the same account as the username.
hint.other: See the server response below and the API log for details: docker compose logs api.
hint.unreadable: The saved password could not be decrypted (the server’s encryption key changed). Enter the password again and save.

mailTest.sourceEnv: The server’s .env values are in use right now. What you save here takes their place.
mailTest.secureHelp: Turn on for port 465; leave off for 587 (STARTTLS is used automatically).
mailTest.passwordHelp: For Gmail use a 16-letter “App password”, not your normal password (you can paste it with spaces).
mailTest.fromHelp: The name and address recipients see. With Gmail the address must match the username.
mailTest.resetDone: Saved settings removed; the server’s .env values will be used.

appUrl.title: Application address
appUrl.help: Links in emails (invitations, password resets, notifications) are built from this address. Enter the address people type in their browser; if it is wrong the links will not open.
appUrl.label: Address
appUrl.hint: Example: https://seyir.company.com or http://192.168.1.20:8092 (no trailing slash needed).
appUrl.resetDone: Saved address removed; the server’s APP_URL will be used.
appUrl.mismatchTitle: Links in emails may point to the wrong address.
appUrl.mismatch: Links are currently built with {{saved}}, but you are using the app at {{here}}. If they differ, an invited person who clicks the link gets a “site can’t be reached” error.

emailSettings.subtitle: Ticket system: incoming emails become Bugs. Manage the mailbox, company details, customer reply texts, companies and project routing rules here.
emailSettings.mailboxHint: Emails to this mailbox become Bugs; replies to customers are sent from this address. The password is stored encrypted and never shown.
emailSettings.fromEnv: The server setting (.env) is in use. Saving makes the values on this screen effective.
emailSettings.smtpHint: If empty, the IMAP server is used.
emailSettings.passwordSet: Saved — type a new password to change it
emailSettings.passwordHint: Leave empty to keep the saved password.
emailSettings.orgHint: Used in reply templates as {sirketAdi}, {telefon}, {web} and {imza}.
emailSettings.signatureHint: If empty, built from company name, phone and website.
emailSettings.templatesHint: Edit or turn off the text of each stage. The preview uses sample data.
emailSettings.subject: Subject

tplWhen.ack: Sent right away when the email becomes a Bug.
tplWhen.processing: Sent when the Bug is converted to a Task, put in a sprint and assigned to someone.
tplWhen.resolved: Sent when the Bug or its converted Task is completed.

emailSettings.companiesHint: The company is found from the sender’s domain. Link a subsidiary’s domain to its parent company; the Bug is then shown under the parent’s name.

company.none: No companies yet. Define domains to match emails to companies.
company.name: Company name
company.parentHint: For a subsidiary, its emails count under the parent and go to the parent’s project.
company.domainsHint: One domain per line. Subdomains (mail.company.com) match automatically.
company.confirmRemove: Delete “{{name}}”? Its domains and company-specific rules are deleted too.

emailSettings.rulesHint: If the subject or text contains the keyword, the Bug goes to the chosen project. Rules are tried top to bottom and the first match wins; otherwise the company’s default project is used.
emailSettings.aiHint: When rules and the company default cannot decide the Project, AI picks it from the email content and also suggests the Bug severity and a short summary.
emailSettings.aiKeyHint: Leave empty to keep the saved key. Stored encrypted, never shown.
emailSettings.aiPrivacy: Privacy: only the subject and the first part of the text are sent; email addresses, phone numbers and links are removed, attachments are not sent. If the AI is unsure or fails, the Bug stays in "Unsorted".

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.subtitle: Analyse people and projects in depth, and compare periods and people.
analytics.subtitleSelf: A summary of your own work: finished items, points, hours and the trend over time.
analytics.newPeriod: No data in the previous period
analytics.trendHint: Click a card to change the metric. Rises and falls follow the selected time grain.
analytics.noWork: No finished work or time entries in this range.
analytics.byProjectHint: How much was finished in each project in the range
analytics.estimateHint: Estimated hours of finished items vs hours logged
analytics.estimateRatio: Logged time is {{percent}}% of the estimate.

flow.noHistory: None of the {{done}} items finished in this range has status-change history (old or imported data). Real cycle time could not be computed; only time from creation to done is shown.
flow.partialHistory: Cycle time is computed only from the {{with}} items with status-change history (of {{done}} finished). Items without history count only in total time.
flow.staleSub: In “In progress” with no movement for over 14 days

flow.dwellHint: Average days finished items stayed in each status. Red: the longest wait
flow.noDwell: No finished items with status-change history.
flow.wipHint: Only from items with status-change history ({{tracked}} / {{total}} items)
flow.noWipHistory: No items with status-change history, so past WIP cannot be drawn.
flow.agingHint: Time since the last status change
flow.staleHint: The 10 items in progress whose last status change is the oldest

sprint.title: Sprint depth

sprint.carrySub: Points not finished and moved to the next sprint/Backlog
sprint.none: No active or completed sprint in this range.

sprint.noBurn: No daily data for this sprint (it may not have started).

capacity.note: Capacity is not stored separately: the weekly hours you pick are split across weekdays (Mon–Fri). Time entries have no time of day, so the heatmap shows daily totals.

capacity.overSub: Remaining estimate exceeds 2 weeks of capacity

capacity.unestimated: {{count}} open items have no estimate and are not in the remaining hours
capacity.weeklyChartHint: Bars: hours logged. Dashed line: the team’s weekly capacity
capacity.weekdayChartHint: Which weekdays the team logs the most hours (total)
capacity.heatmapHint: Each square is a day; darker = more hours logged. Last 26 weeks
capacity.noEntries: This person has no time entries in the range.

quality.title: Quality and support
quality.shareSub: Share of opened items that are Bugs
quality.flowHint: Bars: opened and resolved. Orange line: average resolution time (days, right axis)
quality.severityHint: Resolution time and the oldest open Bug. Over 7 days is red for Critical/Major
quality.routingHint: How many emailed Bugs were later moved to another project
quality.routingNote: For rule, company and AI routing a high moved rate signals wrong assignment (red: 30% and up). In “Unsorted” moving is the expected manual step.
quality.companyHint: Companies sending the most Bugs; click a company to list its Bugs
quality.noCompany: No emailed Bugs from a known company.
quality.criticalHint: The 10 open Bugs that have waited the longest
quality.noCritical: No open Critical or Major Bugs.

forecast.note: Forecasts are simple linear estimates from the current pace, not promises: if the pace changes, so does the estimate. Alerts do not judge people; they only show the change versus the previous period.
forecast.risksHint: Most important first; click a row to open the related page

risk.sprint_behind: {{subject}} is behind plan: at this pace about {{value}}% of the sprint will be finished.
risk.critical_waiting: “{{subject}}” has been open for {{value}} days (Critical/Major Bug).
risk.person_slowing: {{subject}}: {{value}} items finished in the last 14 days ({{previous}} in the 14 days before).
risk.project_slowing: {{subject}}: {{value}} items finished in the last 14 days ({{previous}} in the 14 days before).
risk.stuck_items: {{value}} items have been idle in “In progress” for over 14 days.
risk.unassigned_bugs: {{value}} Bugs have been unassigned for over 3 days.

forecast.sprintsHint: Light shade: the level expected by the end date at this pace
forecast.noEstimate: No pointed work in the sprint, so no estimate.
forecast.projection: At this pace {{pct}}% of the total will be finished by sprint end. Remaining work done by: {{finish}}.
forecast.epicsHint: Remaining points ÷ the project’s pace over the last 4 weeks
